systemUnderstanding.purpose: Engineering intelligence for AI-powered software development. Gives AI coding agents a persistent engineering map, mental model, and enforceable guardrails.
systemUnderstanding.businessObjective: Deliver map generation, mental model generation, guardrail enforcement, context retrieval, drift detection, impact analysis and verification for EngineeringOS.
mostImportantConstraints: Dependency rule: entry → application → domain → repository → infrastructure.
No secrets in code; configuration from validated environment.
Tests required for every invariant and critical workflow.

businessRules.statement: map generation must behave predictably: same input, same output, safe under retry and concurrency.
mental model generation must behave predictably: same input, same output, safe under retry and concurrency.
guardrail enforcement must behave predictably: same input, same output, safe under retry and concurrency.
context retrieval must behave predictably: same input, same output, safe under retry and concurrency.
drift detection must behave predictably: same input, same output, safe under retry and concurrency.
impact analysis must behave predictably: same input, same output, safe under retry and concurrency.
verification must behave predictably: same input, same output, safe under retry and concurrency.
No capability may be reached without authentication and authorization.
Repeating any state-changing operation must produce the same result as the first attempt.

invariants.statement: Only authorized principals may read or mutate protected data.
State-changing operations are idempotent: retries never duplicate effects.
Multi-step writes are atomic: no partial state is observable.
Security-relevant actions are written to an audit trail.
enforcement: audit logging on auth and mutation

invariants.statement: No secrets or credentials exist anywhere in the repository.
The engineering model and the codebase never diverge without recorded evidence.
Every implementation file has a corresponding test file.
enforcement: CI: verify test files exist for all source files

invariants.statement: No skipped or pending tests exist in committed code.
Every test contains at least one assertion.
enforcement: CI: lint rule to verify assertions in test blocks

invariants.statement: Test coverage must meet minimum threshold (80% lines).
enforcement: CI: enforce coverage threshold in test runner config

invariants.statement: All services have health check endpoints.
Application version is exposed via /health or /version endpoint.

failureModes.name: Capability service failure
failureModes.description: A capability is unavailable or inconsistent.

failureModes.name: Data store outage
failureModes.description: Persistence is unavailable, blocking reads and writes.

failureModes.name: External provider timeout
failureModes.mitigation: Timeout, retry with backoff, circuit breaker.

failureModes.name: Data inconsistency
failureModes.description: Partial writes or duplicate effects observed.

recoveryStrategies.name: Retry with exponential backoff
recoveryStrategies.description: Transient failures are retried with jitter and bounded attempts.

recoveryStrategies.name: Circuit breaker
recoveryStrategies.description: Failing dependencies trip open and probe recovery.

recoveryStrategies.name: Idempotent replay
recoveryStrategies.description: Consumers replay events without duplicating effects.

recoveryStrategies.name: Rollback to previous artifact
recoveryStrategies.description: Deploys are reversible in one action.

architecturalPrinciples.name: Dependency Rule
architecturalPrinciples.description: Dependencies point inward; entry code never reaches storage directly.

architecturalPrinciples.name: Fail Fast
architecturalPrinciples.description: Validate at boundaries; surface errors immediately with context.

architecturalPrinciples.name: Least Privilege
architecturalPrinciples.description: Every principal and process gets the minimum access required.

architecturalPrinciples.name: Defense in Depth
architecturalPrinciples.description: Security is enforced at entry, service, and data layers simultaneously.

architecturalPrinciples.name: Idempotent by Default
architecturalPrinciples.description: Side effects are safe to retry by construction.

architecturalPrinciples.name: Observed over Assumed
architecturalPrinciples.description: Claims about the system require evidence from code, tests, or runtime.

architecturalPrinciples.name: Keep It Minimal
architecturalPrinciples.description: No speculative abstraction, dependency, or code.

architecturalPrinciples.name: Predictable Structure
architecturalPrinciples.description: Modules, names, and boundaries are consistent and discoverable.

decisions.title: Architecture Style
decisions.context: Initial architecture decision made while generating the EngineeringOS engineering model.
decisions.decision: Adopt clean-architecture architecture with enforced module boundaries.
decisions.reason: Matches the project scale and the goal of a predictable, maintainable codebase.
consequences: Modules may be extracted to services later
decisions.confidenceReason: Generated from onboarding input; revisit and accept as code is written.

decisions.title: Idempotency Strategy
decisions.context: Initial architecture decision made while generating the EngineeringOS engineering model.
decisions.decision: State-changing endpoints accept an idempotency key and return the stored result on retry.
decisions.reason: Makes retries and webhook replays safe, which is essential for payments and external systems.
decisions.confidenceReason: Generated from onboarding input; revisit and accept as code is written.

decisions.title: Error Handling
decisions.context: Initial architecture decision made while generating the EngineeringOS engineering model.
decisions.decision: Use explicit typed errors and fail-fast validation; no empty catches.
decisions.reason: Makes failures predictable and diagnosable across the system.
decisions.confidenceReason: Generated from onboarding input; revisit and accept as code is written.

decisions.title: Observability
decisions.context: Initial architecture decision made while generating the EngineeringOS engineering model.
decisions.decision: Structured JSON logging via the observability module; console logging banned in production paths.
decisions.reason: Enables diagnosis without guesswork and keeps PII out of logs.
decisions.confidenceReason: Generated from onboarding input; revisit and accept as code is written.

decisions.title: Configuration
decisions.context: Initial architecture decision made while generating the EngineeringOS engineering model.
decisions.decision: All configuration is validated at startup from the environment; secrets never enter the repository.
decisions.reason: Keeps secrets out of code and catches misconfiguration early.
consequences: Environment must be complete to boot
decisions.confidenceReason: Generated from onboarding input; revisit and accept as code is written.

assumptions.statement: The listed primary users (developers, tech leads and AI coding agents) accurately represent who uses the system.
The critical capabilities (map generation, mental model generation, guardrail enforcement, context retrieval, drift detection, impact analysis and verification) define the complete initial scope.
Build proceeds from the current workspace state; existing code must be reconciled with the model.
A single deployable artifact hosts all capabilities with separate modules.

unknowns.question: What are the most critical business workflows and their exact failure modes?
What load and concurrency are expected at launch?
What compliance and regulatory requirements apply?
What are the exact contracts of external systems (payment, notification, auth providers)?
What is the release cadence and who operates the system?

constraints.statement: All code is type-safe; no `any` at module boundaries.
Secrets and credentials never appear in code or generated files.
Automated tests are mandatory for new behavior and every invariant.
The dependency rule is enforced by guardrails; violations block merge.
Public APIs stay backward compatible unless a new version is introduced.
Every committed change passes lint, typecheck, tests, and EngineeringOS verification.

currentState.summary: Initial model generated from onboarding; no code verified yet.

intendedState.summary: Production-grade EngineeringOS with verified invariants, automated tests, and a green EngineeringOS verification.

risks.name: Architectural drift
risks.description: Changes may violate the intended architecture over time.
risks.mitigation: EngineeringOS guardrails, drift detection, and regular verification.

risks.name: Supply-chain dependency risk
risks.description: A vulnerable or abandoned dependency may undermine security.
risks.mitigation: Pin versions, scan dependencies, and review before adding new packages.

risks.name: Data integrity under concurrency
risks.description: Concurrent writes may cause lost updates or partial states.
risks.mitigation: Transactions, optimistic locking, and idempotency keys.

risks.name: Scaling beyond design assumptions
risks.description: Growth may exceed the capacity of a single artifact or store.
risks.mitigation: Stateless services, cacheable reads, and partitioned data stores.

risks.name: Security debt from unguarded changes
risks.description: Expedient AI-generated changes may skip auth or leak secrets.
risks.mitigation: Security guardrails, secret scanning, and security review in Definition of Done.

risks.name: External gateway single point of failure
risks.description: Payment/notification provider outages degrade core flows.
risks.mitigation: Timeouts, retries with backoff, circuit breakers, and degraded-mode responses.
